result:
The proposed answer α = −1/2 looks wrong, mainly because of a lower bound that it contradicts.

**Lower bound from cut points.** A cut time t has no loop covering it, so it survives loop erasure in any order. The number of cut times up to n is therefore a lower bound on the LLF length. In d = 4, Lawler's cut-time results give density (log n)^{−1/3}, the same exponent as chronological loop-erased walk. If so, the LLF length is at least n(log n)^{−1/3+o(1)}, which forces α ≥ −1/3 and rules out −1/2.

**The proposed solution's own inputs.** It sets the cut-point density at (log n)^{−1/2}, citing the two-walk non-intersection probability. That is the wrong quantity. Two independent walks not intersecting is not the same as a single walk having a cut time, and the proposal does not justify identifying the two. Its heuristic that contacts "almost always kill" with probability 1 − O(1/k) per scale is also asserted rather than derived, so the product estimate is unsupported.

**Consistency check.** The proposal says LLF is "maximally destructive, saturating the cut-point bound." If the cut-point density is (log n)^{−1/3}, that saturation would give −1/3, not −1/2. The argument is internally inconsistent with the standard d = 4 value.

I am not certain of the exact value of α, and I do not recall the precise published exponent for LLF. But the cut-point lower bound is a strong structural argument, and it excludes −1/2 given the known d = 4 cut-time exponent.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 3
